assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns small molecules into tools that recruit E3 ligases to remove proteins, opening targets that inhibitors cannot reach. The concept is original, the chemistry is clear, and structural work on ternary complexes and the cereblon-thalidomide mechanism gives an unusually well-grounded molecular explanation. Clinical degraders are advancing.
assessment.attribution: The PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies and co-workers) and the identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target (Handa, Ito) are two distinct pillars; Ciulli's VHL ligands and structural work are also decisive. A three-person prize cannot cover all of these fairly.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of independent confirmation, many degraders in clinical trials, and a first-in-class clinical readout; recognition is timely. Long-term clinical outcomes remain open.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on PROTACs or on molecular glues (cereblon).
Credit split among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Sakamoto and Ito is unresolved.
Clinical benefit of degraders is still being established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another at a programmed site without double-strand breaks, an inventive marriage of deaminase chemistry and programmable targeting. The impact on research and on emerging therapies is large and the concept is clean.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu led the invention and the follow-on work (cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead authors). Nishida and Kondo made an independent early deaminase-based fusion. A prize to Liu alone is defensible; broader credit is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently in many labs and organisms; first clinical editing results exist. Possibly early for the chemistry committee given the 2020 CRISPR prize and overlap with prime editing (B061).
uncertainties: Whether the committee views genome editing as chemistry or as overlapping the earlier CRISPR prize.
Treatment of the independent Nishida and Kondo work.
Long-term clinical safety evidence is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar-cell efficiency from a few percent to over 25 percent in a decade, with a defect-tolerant, solution-processable material family that also reaches LEDs and detectors. A materials chemistry advance with clear function-from-structure logic.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used the perovskite as a sensitizer (2009); Park and Gratzel (2012) and Snaith (2012) established the solid-state device. Kanatzidis, Seok and Gratzel also have strong claims, so any three-person selection is contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiencies are independently certified worldwide, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercial durability are unresolved, so the technology is still maturing.
uncertainties: Operational stability and toxicity may limit real-world impact.
Credit among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis is disputed.
Whether the stability problem makes recognition premature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and related molecular sieves, through organic structure-directing agents, new framework types and engineered active sites, underpins industrial catalysis and adsorption. As a structural chemist of porous materials I regard the combination of synthesis, structure solution and function as a field-defining achievement; I note my own proximity to the field.
assessment.attribution: Zones (SSZ-13 and Chevron structure-directing agents), Corma (ITQ materials, catalyst design) and Davis (new frameworks and Sn-beta) made major, separable contributions; Yu (open-framework materials) and Tsapatsis (nanosheets, membranes) are also credited. The set is broad and the individual contributions overlap.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and large-scale industrial use (fluid cracking, NOx abatement). Very mature. Not a single discovery but a body of work, and the 2025 prize on MOFs reduces the case for another porous-materials award soon.
uncertainties: Compound discovery with diffuse attribution.
Possible overlap with the recent MOF prize.
I may be biased by my own field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large family of 2D transition-metal carbides and nitrides made by selective etching of MAX phases, with tunable composition and properties for energy storage, EMI shielding and catalysis. It is a genuinely new materials family with a clear structural definition.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum published the first Ti3C2 MXene in 2011 (Drexel); the three-person configuration is natural and reasonably clean.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly growing field with strong confirmation of structure, but practical applications are still emerging and the discovery is relatively recent.
uncertainties: Real-world application impact is not yet established.
Maturity: about fifteen years since discovery.
Many composition claims rest on averaged characterization.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers determines structures from micro- and nanocrystals and resolves time-dependent dynamics, bypassing radiation damage. It is an enabling method that opened a whole class of structures, closely related in spirit to my own crystallographic work with tiny crystals.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the 2011 proof of principle; Fromme (photosystem I crystals) and Hajdu (diffract-before-destroy concept) were central; Schlichting contributed time-resolved mechanisms. Credit is plausible for three but leaves out significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced at multiple XFELs and used for membrane proteins and time-resolved studies. The facilities are rare, and routine impact is smaller than that of synchrotron and cryo-EM methods.
uncertainties: Restricted access to XFEL facilities limits breadth of impact.
Credit among Chapman, Fromme, Hajdu, Schlichting is not uniquely resolved.
Competition from microED and cryo-EM for small crystals.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The dye-sensitized nanocrystalline solar cell introduced a mesoscopic, molecular approach to photovoltaics and inspired later perovskite devices. The 1991 concept was original and clearly demonstrated.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 Nature paper by O'Regan and Gratzel is the clear anchor, with Hagfeldt a later key contributor. A two-person prize is supportable.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and heavily confirmed, but commercial impact has been modest compared with silicon and perovskites, which weakens lasting-impact arguments.
uncertainties: Limited commercial deployment.
Gratzel also appears under perovskites (B054), so one person may be counted twice.
Hagfeldt's role relative to O'Regan.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Non-contact AFM with CO-functionalized tips resolves the bond structure of individual molecules and has been used to identify products of on-surface reactions. As a structural chemist I appreciate a direct, interpretable atomic-resolution structure measurement.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl (qPlus sensor), Gross and Meyer (2009 Science molecular imaging) are the main contributors; Eigler and Ho are linked to related scanning-probe work, which complicates the credit.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across many laboratories and used in on-surface synthesis. Applications are specialized to ultra-high-vacuum surfaces, so the impact on mainstream chemistry is narrower.
uncertainties: Limited generality (vacuum, surface-bound molecules).
Overlap with the 1986 physics prize for scanning probe microscopies.
Credit with Eigler and Ho unresolved.
